rationale: sphereflake is a small (7 functions, ~6.5KB text), floating-point-heavy recursive ray tracer whose hot code (main, create, node_t::intersect) executes in tight loops, so cost dimensions are weighted high enough to keep BCF/FLA selective rather than blanket-applied: both inflate code size substantially on tiny binaries and add per-iteration overhead on FP-intensive render loops, while their correctness risk stays low since control-flow transforms do not alter FP semantics. SUB is favored broadly (cheap instruction substitution, low risk, good diversity across the arithmetic-heavy vector math in basis_t and v_t helpers), and SPLIT acts as a cheap force-multiplier that enlarges basic-block graphs for BCF/FLA to scramble, so it gets high diversity weight with negligible cost/risk. IBR and ICALL receive solid security/diversity weights because flattening the call/branch structure of the recursive create and templated intersect instantiations resists static call-graph recovery, but their RuntimeCost and CorrectnessRisk weights are elevated since indirect dispatch on hot paths and through C++ template/member calls can cost real cycles and occasionally misfire on virtual/exception edges. IGV is kept with moderate weights: the program has limited global state, so its payoff is modest but its indirect-global references cheaply harden data-target recovery, gated by a higher correctness weight for the C++ static-init paths.
